## Goal / symptom
A WSL2 toolkit contributor does not yet have one canonical, repeatable loop for bootstrapping the workspace, running the game against a locally edited `rulebooks/dnd5e` module, seeding reusable characters through production APIs, and launching a minimal live sandbox through the normal game flow.

## Desired outcome
Deliver an explicit `game-dev` bootstrap/start/refresh/seed/status/down workflow that supports one active development scenario. A contributor can edit the local D&D 5e rulebook, explicitly refresh the running stack, seed a reusable Protection Fighter and Barbarian, assemble either one character or both in either order on a preloaded Dungeon Builder canvas, save it, and enter it through the real lobby and normal GameView paths.

Keep the MVP narrow: one canvas template and one active scenario, not a generic scenario framework or catalog.

## Contract boundaries
- `game-dev` owns the WSL2 contributor workflow: bootstrap, start, explicit refresh, seed, status, and down. Automatic file watching is out of scope.
- `rpg-api` supports a local override of exactly one toolkit module, `rulebooks/dnd5e`. The MVP requires no `rpg-toolkit` code change.
- `rpg-api/cmd/sandboxseed` calls the running real `CharacterService` APIs. Character creation must use the currently implemented production section path: `CreateDraft`, `UpdateName`, `UpdateRace`, `UpdateClass`, `UpdateBackground`, `UpdateAbilityScores` (including class choices), `GetDraft`, `FinalizeDraft`, and `ListCharacters`/`DeleteCharacter` where needed for idempotency. It uses the existing equip API to equip the fighter's shield.
- `GetRequirements` and `SubmitChoices` handlers are currently unimplemented. Completing those generic handlers is not part of this MVP and must not become a prerequisite.
- The web adds a dev-only sandbox entry that reuses Dungeon Builder with one preloaded canvas template, accepts one or two characters owned by the current user in either order, persists through `PutDungeon`, and uses the real lobby create/join/ready/start APIs.
- Launch uses normal GameView links; optional harness links may supplement but not replace that path.
- Preserve production auth and ownership checks. Do not construct `Character.Data` directly and do not write directly to Redis.
- Non-goals: native-Windows asset setup, proto changes, deployment changes unless later proven necessary, arbitrary scenario catalogs, weakened auth/ownership, and direct Redis or character-data construction.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A clean WSL2 environment can bootstrap and run the documented `game-dev` bootstrap/start/status/down loop.
- [ ] After a local `rulebooks/dnd5e` edit, an explicit refresh makes the running API use that local module.
- [ ] Seeding is API-based and idempotent: repeated runs create or reuse exactly the intended reusable Protection Fighter and Barbarian, with the fighter shield equipped through the real equip API.
- [ ] The dev-only sandbox opens Dungeon Builder with the single preloaded canvas template and saves it through `PutDungeon`.
- [ ] The saved sandbox completes the real lobby create/join/ready/start flow with a single-seat Fighter party.
- [ ] The same flow succeeds with a single-seat Barbarian party.
- [ ] The same flow succeeds with a two-seat Fighter → Barbarian party.
- [ ] The same flow succeeds with a two-seat Barbarian → Fighter party.
- [ ] Every accepted composition reaches the normal GameView path; optional harness links are not required for success.
- [ ] Verification proves that execution came from the local `rulebooks/dnd5e` override rather than the published module.

## Verification evidence
- Capture a clean-WSL2 command transcript covering bootstrap, start, status, explicit refresh after a local rulebook edit, seed, and down.
- Capture two consecutive seed runs plus `ListCharacters` output showing stable reuse/no duplicates, both required characters, and the fighter's shield; retain API logs or traces showing CharacterService and equip API calls rather than direct storage writes.
- Record the saved Dungeon Builder template and the resulting dungeon identifier, then exercise the four party/order cases through the real lobby APIs into normal GameView.
- Include deterministic evidence tied to the local rulebook edit (for example, a unique local-only behavior or instrumented version value observed through the running API) that distinguishes the override from the published module.
- Report focused automated tests and repository CI for each eventual implementation PR, including evidence that auth and ownership remain enforced.

## Related / dependencies
This is the canonical cross-repository umbrella and Project 19 routing item. Design approval is the next gate. Do not create repository implementation issues, branches, or PRs until that design is approved; after approval, create only the owning-repository issues needed for the bounded `game-dev`, `rpg-api`, and `rpg-dnd5e-web` work.

The loop depends on the existing production CharacterService section APIs, existing equip API, Dungeon Builder/`PutDungeon`, lobby create/join/ready/start APIs, and normal GameView routing. Deployment work is excluded unless implementation evidence later proves it necessary.

— asset-pipeline agent, on behalf of KirkDiggler
